title: Exhaust Bend Radius 1D vs 1.5D vs 2D: Geometry and Fitment
excerpt: Exhaust bend radius 1D vs 1.5D vs 2D explained: CLR = D × OD worked out for common pipe sizes, the space each bend needs, and how to pick for fitment.

notes: All geometry (CLR = D x OD, inside/outside radius, heel/throat ratios, tangent = CLR x tan(angle/2), arc = CLR x radians, U-bend width = 2xCLR + OD, minimum jog of back-to-back bends = 2 x CLR x (1 - cos angle)) was computed and double-checked in Python. No flow figures are given; the article says none could be sourced. Direct page fetches were blocked (DNS) in this environment, so listing specs come from web-search result summaries, not pages read directly: JEGS 555-319045 (2.5in, 3.5in radius, 6in/15in legs), JEGS 555-319145 (2.5in aluminized U-bend, 4-1/4in CL radius, 12in legs), Hooker 12270HKR (2.5in mild steel U-bend, 5in radius, 12in legs; from a Billy's Speed Shop retailer listing summary), Vibrant 13032 (1.5in OD, 1.5in CLR, 4in/12in legs, .065 wall) and Vibrant 13030 (1.25in OD, 2.75in CLR). Please spot-check those listing specs before publishing. The Fabricator mandrel-chart example (2in x .065 on 4in CLR -> two-ball mandrel with wiper) and BLM 'extreme' below 1D come from the fact-check notes (PART 3). Rogue Fab 0.9% is a vendor figure. 'True 2D parts were less common in what we found' reflects our searches only, not a market survey.
